title: Momentum
page_title: Momentum | Edexcel International A Level (IAL) Physics Revision Notes 2018

blocks.md: - Linear momentum (*p*) is defined as the product of mass and velocity

blocks.alt: Linear momentum equation, downloadable AS & A Level Physics revision notes

blocks.md: ***Momentum is the product of mass and velocity***

- Momentum is a vector quantity - it has both a magnitude and a direction
- This means it can have a negative or positive value

  - If an object travelling to the right has positive momentum, an object travelling to the left (in the opposite direction) has a negative momentum
- The SI unit for momentum is **kg m s**<sup>**−1**</sup>

blocks.alt: Negative momentum, downloadable AS & A Level Physics revision notes

blocks.md: ***When the ball is travelling in the opposite direction, its velocity is negative. Since momentum = mass × velocity, its momentum is also negative***

blocks.label: Worked Example
blocks.md:
Which object has the most momentum?

![WE - Momentum comparison question image, downloadable AS & A Level Physics revision notes](assets/a3eba9515c1f-we-momentum-comparison-question-image.png)

**Answer:**

![WE - Momentum comparison answer image, downloadable AS & A Level Physics revision notes](assets/27c505ec1e98-we-momentum-comparison-answer-image.png)

- Both the tennis ball and the brick have the same momentum
- Even though the brick is much heavier than the ball, the ball is travelling much faster than the brick
- This means that on impact, they would both exert a similar force (depending on the time it takes for each to come to rest)

blocks.label: Exam Hint
blocks.md:
Since momentum is in** kg m s**<sup>**−1**</sup>:

- If the mass is given in grams, make sure to convert to kg by dividing the value by 1000.
- If the velocity is given in km s<sup>−1</sup>, make sure to convert to m s<sup>−1</sup> by multiplying the value by 1000

The direction you consider positive is your choice, as long the signs of the numbers (positive or negative) are consistent  throughout the question.

Sketching a diagram **which includes the signs on positive and negative values** will help you avoid mistakes when calculating
